widget.solution:
import math
from collections import Counter

def letter_entropy(path):
    """Bits per symbol of the names in path, one stream with an end mark per name."""
    names = open(path).read().splitlines()
    stream = "".join(name + "." for name in names)
    counts = Counter(stream)
    n = len(stream)
    h = -sum(c / n * math.log2(c / n) for c in counts.values())
    return round(h, 4)

explain.text: $228{,}146 \times 3.5412 = 807{,}911$ bits, and $\div 8$ gives 100,989 bytes, about 101 thousand. A better model of the text gives a shorter code. The 4.0723 of the letter counts is the floor only for codes that treat each symbol on its own; a model that uses the previous letter has a lower floor.

screens.prose: Every time, a model gave each symbol a chance $q$, and a code built on it spent $-\log_2 q$ bits on it. Averaged over the text, that cost is least when $q$ matches the text's own shares, and then it equals their entropy. A model that predicts the text better gives a shorter code.

ideas: The entropy of a text's symbol counts is the least a code built on those counts averages: 4.0723 bits for the names, against 4.7549 for equal chances.
A better model, such as one that knows the previous letter, gives a shorter code: 3.5412 bits.
A general compressor such as zlib knows nothing about the text in advance, so a good model can beat it.
